title: What a plant takes in and gives out
subject: Life science

sources.title: NGSS 5-LS1-1: Support an argument that plants get the materials they need for growth chiefly from air and water
OpenStax Biology 2e, 30.2 Stems (stomata take up carbon dioxide and release oxygen and water vapor)
OpenStax Biology 2e, 25.1 Early Plant Life (roots take up water and minerals)
OpenStax Biology 2e, 31.3 Nutritional Adaptations of Plants

note.text: Plants need sunlight. Light gives them the energy to make their own food.
Light spreads out from the sun in every direction, and some reaches the plant's leaves.
Above the ground, leaves meet the air and light. Below, roots meet the soil and water.

steps.title: Stem and leaves
steps.instruction: Trace the stem and the two leaves.

note.text: Leaves have tiny openings that let air in and out. That's where the plant takes in carbon dioxide.
note.remember: Leaves trade gases with the air.

note.text: Roots take up water, plus small amounts of minerals, from the soil. They also anchor the plant.

steps.title: Sunlight
steps.instruction: Draw the arrow of sunlight reaching the leaf.

note.text: Sunlight brings energy, not matter. It powers the leaf's food-making.

steps.title: Carbon dioxide in
steps.instruction: Draw the arrow of carbon dioxide going into the leaf.

note.text: Carbon dioxide is a gas in the air. The plant builds it, with water, into sugar: food and new plant material.
note.remember: In from the air: carbon dioxide.

steps.title: Water in
steps.instruction: Draw the arrow of water going into the roots.

note.text: Water travels from the roots up the stem to the leaves.

steps.title: Oxygen out
steps.instruction: Draw the arrow of oxygen leaving the leaf.

note.text: As it makes food, the plant gives off oxygen into the air. Water vapor escapes from the leaves too.

steps.title: Label the arrows
steps.instruction: Pick the right name for each numbered arrow.

targets.role: Gas taken in from the air.

mistakes.Oxygen: This arrow points into the leaf. The plant takes in carbon dioxide and gives out oxygen.

targets.role: Gas given out to the air.

mistakes.Carbon dioxide: This arrow points out of the leaf. The plant gives off oxygen.

commonMistakes.Soil: Soil gives a plant small amounts of minerals, but these arrows show light, gases and water.

steps.title: Argue
steps.instruction: Where does a plant's material come from?
steps.question: A tiny seed grows into a huge tree. Where did most of the tree's new material come from?

options.feedback: Yes. The tree builds itself mostly from carbon dioxide in the air and water, using the sun's energy.
Surprisingly, no. Soil gives only small amounts of minerals. Most of the tree is built from air and water.
Sunlight gives the energy, but it isn't matter. The material comes from air and water.
The seed was tiny. Almost all the tree's material came later, from air and water.

steps.title: Give and take
steps.question: Which gas does the plant take in, and which does it give out?

options.text: Takes in carbon dioxide, gives out oxygen
options.feedback: Right. Leaves take in carbon dioxide to make food and give off oxygen.

options.text: Takes in oxygen, gives out carbon dioxide
options.feedback: That's the other way round. To make food, leaves take in carbon dioxide and give off oxygen.

options.text: Takes in water, gives out sunlight
options.feedback: Sunlight comes from the sun. The gases are carbon dioxide in and oxygen out.
Plants do: they take in carbon dioxide and give off oxygen through their leaves.
